## 1. Load the synthetic SBP data

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
trial <- read.csv("sbp-demo.csv")
stopifnot(nrow(trial) == 60L, !anyDuplicated(trial$id))
names(trial)
```

The data have one row per patient and SBP at baseline, 6 weeks, and 12 weeks.
The analysis uses `sbp_0` and `sbp_12`, with treatment group in `arm`.

## 2. Original candidates and my prediction

These are **prepared teaching examples**, not a transcript of an AI response.
The plain code blocks below are preserved for review and do not execute.

Plot candidate:

```r
p <- ggplot(trial, aes(sbp_0, sbp_12)) + geom_point()
```

Summary candidate:

```r
# Requested: total n, observed n, mean and SD of week-12 SBP by arm.
trial |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(sbp_12)) |>
  dplyr::summarise(n = dplyr::n(), mean_sbp = mean(sbp_12),
                 sd_sbp = sd(sbp_12), .by = arm)
```

## 5. Independent verification

Run these supplied checks yourself. Compare their output with the revised plot
and summary. Keep these checks unchanged when requesting the revision.

```{r}
# Pair count: count eligible rows instead of counting visible dots.
sum(complete.cases(trial[c("sbp_0", "sbp_12")]))
sum(!complete.cases(trial[c("sbp_0", "sbp_12")]))

# Independent base-R checks for total and observed counts.
table(trial$arm)
with(trial, tapply(!is.na(sbp_12), arm, sum))

# Compare these means with the corrected summary as well.
with(trial, tapply(sbp_12, arm, mean, na.rm = TRUE))
```

**My verification:** Report the pair count, total counts, and observed counts.
Explain why total and observed n differ. Confirm the plot's axes and colors,
and whether the independently calculated means match. Note any correction
you made after reviewing the assistant's work.
